title: Strings and the command line: cheat sheet

blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.body: A string is a char array that ends in `'\0'`. Headers `string.h` and `ctype.h` work on strings and chars. `argv` gives you words from the command line, and `fgets` reads a line safely.

blocks.title: string.h
items: `strcmp(a, b)`: 0 when equal, sign gives the order
`strcpy(d, s)` and `strcat(d, s)`: d needs room

blocks.title: main with arguments
Read a line
argc and argv
items: `argv[1]` is the first argument, as text

blocks.body: Check `argc` before reading `argv`, and give `fgets` the buffer's real size.
